failure.repairHint: Repair is independent of ABC / AABBCC and ordinary retry rules. Each target can be repaired and resent immediately once, within the total attempt limit. Errors after repair follow the error rules.
failure.thinkingSignatureRecoveryHint: For Claude Anthropic requests with thinking signature errors, convert historical thinking to text, remove encrypted thinking, and disable thinking before resending. Repair once per target, independently of retry order, quota, backoff and HTTP error rules. Counts toward the total attempt limit.
failure.openaiReasoningRecovery: Retry after Codex / OpenAI reasoning repair
failure.openaiReasoningRecoveryHint: On explicit Responses reasoning ciphertext or item errors, remove invalid ciphertext or repair the identified item while preserving readable summaries, tool calls and conversation bindings. Repair once per target, independently of ordinary retry rules, within the total attempt limit. Invalid compaction ciphertext is returned as an error.
failure.openaiFunctionOutputRecoveryHint: Off by default. When a Responses request is rejected because function or custom-tool output ciphertext cannot be decrypted, drop those encrypted parts, keep plaintext results, and resend to the same target. Shares one repair per target with reasoning repair and can clear both in the same attempt. Tool call_id pairs stay intact. Independent of ordinary retry rules; counts toward the total attempt limit.
failure.title: Failure handling
failure.serviceHint: Set API provider priority in the API provider list. Error handling inherits defaults unless overridden here.
failure.maxRetriesHint: Excludes the first request and repair requests. 0 disables ordinary retries; maximum 5.
failure.backoffHint: Repeated failures increase the delay, up to 60,000 ms. Longer upstream waits use a backup when switching is allowed.
failure.timeoutHint: 0 means unlimited. This only limits waiting for response headers, not a long reply already streaming.
failure.retryRulesHint: When enabled, continue with the configured retry strategy. Otherwise, return the error.
failure.otherErrors: Enabled request repairs run independently first. If repair is unavailable or fails, error rules apply. Unlisted HTTP errors are returned directly. Replies that have started are never retried, repaired or switched.
failure.invalid: Check retry counts, delays, and error rules. The maximum delay must not be shorter than the first delay.
failure.serviceSummary: Permitted errors get up to {{count}} extra attempts, initially waiting about {{delay}} ms.
failure.maxAttemptsHint: Includes the first request, ordinary retries, repair requests, and backups: 1–20 total.
failure.globalSwitch: Allow switching API providers after failure
failure.globalOffHint: When automatic switching is off, a failed request does not try another API provider.
failure.loadFailed: Could not load the default policy.

routing.identityHint: Enabled by default and controlled independently. Changes save automatically and apply to new requests without restarting. When disabled, recognized client identities are preserved; unknown clients use the default identity. Authentication and required protocol headers still apply.
routing.codexIdentityHint: Unify User-Agent, originator, and version, and drop other SDK fingerprint headers. They remain paired when disabled.
routing.claudeIdentityHint: Unify the Claude Code User-Agent and SDK fingerprint headers (X-Stainless). Preserve client feature betas and add required OAuth betas.
routing.grokIdentityHint: Unify the Grok CLI User-Agent and version. They remain paired when disabled.
routing.protectionHint: Applies to Claude and Codex subscriptions. Enabled by default and controlled independently. Changes save automatically and apply to new requests.

protection.officialPassthroughHint: When a genuine Claude Code or Codex CLI request is recognized, add only credentials and required OAuth items and forward it unchanged, without rewriting the body, identity headers, or session identifiers. The other protections then apply only to third-party and converted requests. When disabled, every subscription request is shaped by the rules below.
protection.risk: Detect upstream risk control and pause scheduling
protection.riskHint: Detect suspension, exhausted quota, and rejection signals, pause the affected account, and fail over to another API provider. Refresh the token once on 401. When disabled, upstream errors are only forwarded, not recorded or paused. Paused accounts still need to be resumed from the API provider list.
protection.codexRequestsHint: Shape parameters like the Codex CLI: disable storage, add instructions, drop sampling and output-limit parameters subscriptions reject, and stream non-streaming requests before aggregating the result. When disabled, native requests are forwarded unchanged and converted requests get only required fixes.
protection.claudeRequestsHint: Fix structure only, never content: limit cache breakpoints, resolve thinking and sampling conflicts, add max_tokens, and drop empty text blocks and unsigned thinking blocks. Converted requests keep only Claude Code betas. When disabled, only the Claude Code system prompt is added.
protection.sessionIsolationHint: Map session IDs, prompt_cache_key, and metadata.user_id to stable values unique to each account, so one conversation failing over is not linked across accounts. When disabled, client session identifiers are forwarded unchanged.

routing.learningHint: When AstrLink must supply a subscription client identity itself (converted requests, model discovery, connection tests, authorization, and quota requests), it uses the identity learned from official client requests, or the built-in identity until one is learned. Only newer versions are accepted, and they persist across restarts. Official client requests forwarded unchanged are not affected. Changes save automatically and apply to new requests.

learning.codex: Learn identity from Codex CLI requests
learning.codexHint: Record the User-Agent, originator, and version of recognized Codex CLI requests. When disabled, the built-in identity is used; a learned identity is kept but no longer used.
learning.claude: Learn identity from Claude Code requests
learning.claudeHint: Record the User-Agent and SDK fingerprint headers (X-Stainless) of recognized Claude Code requests. When disabled, the built-in identity is used; a learned identity is kept but no longer used.
learning.codexVersionHint: A version newer than the current identity replaces the version in User-Agent and version; an older one never downgrades it. Must be 0.144.0 or newer.
learning.codexVersionInvalid: Enter version 0.144.0 or newer, such as 0.160.0.
learning.claudeVersionHint: A version newer than the current identity replaces the version in User-Agent; an older one never downgrades it.
learning.versionPlaceholder: Leave empty to use the learned or built-in version

guide.title: Change the model, keep the client as it is
guide.description: Follow the request to the right, then the response back to the left.
guide.flow: The request goes right to the API provider and the response returns left. Redirection replaces only the outgoing model name; the response passes through unchanged.

modelRedirect.helpMatch: When a client requests a model whose name exactly matches the requested model (case-sensitive), the target model is used to select API providers and forward the request.
modelRedirect.helpSingleHop: Redirects apply once: the target model is not matched against other rules, so another rule's requested model cannot be a target.
modelRedirect.helpResponse: Only the model name in the request sent to the API provider is rewritten. Responses, streamed output, and errors pass through exactly as the provider returns them, so they name the model actually called. Request records and trajectories mark the redirect.
modelRedirect.helpDisabled: Disabled rules are kept but not applied.
modelRedirect.helpAuto: Clients still using {{model}} can be redirected to another model. {{model}} cannot be a target model.
modelRedirect.emptyHint: Forward a client's requested model as another model, for example to keep an old model name working or to replace a retired model.
modelRedirect.targetUnlisted: No enabled API provider lists {{model}}. Make sure an API provider supports it.

builtinTools.title: Responses tool mapping
builtinTools.upstreamHint: Uses the selected provider’s Responses API. The executor model calls the same type of built-in tool, and the result returns to the original request’s main model.
builtinTools.externalSearchHint: Uses a Tavily-compatible API for searches, page reads and text lookups. Connects through the API base URL and separately saved key below.
builtinTools.externalImagesHint: Uses an OpenAI Images-compatible API to generate or edit images. Connects through the API base URL and separately saved key below.
builtinTools.serviceImagesHint: Uses the selected provider’s Images API to generate or edit images, reusing that provider’s configured key and proxy.
builtinTools.searchModelHint: Select a chat model supporting the Responses web_search tool, such as the gpt-5 series. This model searches; the original request’s main model continues answering with the results.
builtinTools.imageExecutorHint: Select a chat model supporting the Responses image_generation tool, such as the gpt-5 series. It calls the image tool. To specify an image model such as gpt-image directly, map to an Images API.
builtinTools.serviceImageModelHint: Select an image model supported by this Images API, such as gpt-image-1. This model produces images; the original request’s main model continues the conversation.
builtinTools.testHint: Runs a real tool call; charges may apply.
builtinTools.description: Matches the type field of entries in the tools array of OpenAI Responses requests. When enabled, the gateway exposes the matching tools to the main model as functions, executes their calls through the model or API configured here, and returns the results so the main model can continue. The main model must support function calling.
builtinTools.noProviders: No enabled provider supports native Responses. Configure one under API providers first.
builtinTools.noImageProviders: No enabled OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible, or New API provider. Configure one under API providers first.
